key_insight: Single-number success metrics mask critical operational flaws. The paper proposes treating agent reliability as a multi-dimensional science (consistency, robustness, predictability, and bounded error severity) rather than a single scalar score.
problem_solved: Current evaluations compress agent behavior into one metric, obscuring run-to-run variability, sensitivity to perturbations, whether failures are predictable, and how severe errors can be — all of which matter in deployment.
method: Decompose reliability into four measurable dimensions: consistency (repeatability), robustness (perturbation resistance), predictability of failures, and error-severity bounds.
Define evaluation protocols and metrics that measure agents across multiple runs, controlled perturbations, and failure-triggering conditions.
Apply statistical diagnostics and visualizations (e.g., distributions, CDFs, conditional analyses) to characterize failure modes and quantify worst-case/bounded errors.
impact: Provides practitioners with actionable diagnostics to choose, tune, and monitor agents for real-world deployment, reducing surprise failures and improving operational safety and trustworthiness.
visual_elements: Radar chart comparing agents across the four reliability dimensions (consistency, robustness, predictability, severity bound).
CDF or violin plots of performance across runs and under perturbations to show variability and tail risks.
Heatmap or spaghetti plot of run-to-run trajectories highlighting inconsistent behaviors and outlier failures.
Annotated flow showing predictable vs. unpredictable failure modes and a bar indicating bounded error thresholds.
paper_title: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability
paper_authors: Stephan Rabanser, Sayash Kapoor, Peter Kirgis, Kangheng Liu, Saiteja Utpala
